I know some on the right are portraying criticism of the Iran war as a mainstream media problem but - fact is - some of the hardest questions about U.S. strategic objectives and outcomes are coming from U.S. allies. I hear those doubts here in Israel. Here’s a critique worth listening to from japan, which is of course bearing some of the worst economic costs.


Thomas P (TOM) Logan 🇯🇵 🇺🇸 (@TokyoTom2020)

VIDEO
Former #Japanese #diplomat and foreign policy heavyweight Kunihiko #Miyake didn’t hold
Blasting Iran “back to the stone ages” will not ring kindly to the Iranian people who Trump claimed the war was intended in part to save from their government.
There’s his answer on Iran’s nuclear program: U.S. will monitor it from satellites and hit it if “they make a move.”
First mention of timing: Trump says 2-3 more weeks of war.
Trump once again claims Iran was close to a missile that could reach the U.S. homeland when in fact Intel assessments put that capability years away.
Trump says he “terminated” the 2015 nuclear deal because it sent money to Iran while neglecting to mention he’s allowed Iran to sell billions of dollars in oil just this week.

I’ve been speaking to offcials in Europe and Asia over the last year and they say the same: confidence in the U.S. is already deeply depleted.


Richard N. Haass (@RichardHaass)

I don't know what if anything Pres Trump will say about NATO tonight, but the damage is already done. The reliability at the core of this or any alliance is gone. Europeans no longer have confidence in the American pledge to come to their defense.
